This appeal is directed against the judgment dated 21.07.2008 in a reference, titled, Pritam Singh and others vs. Collector Land Acquisition and another passed by the court of learned Principal District Judge, Udhampur (hereinafter to be referred as the reference court), whereby the compensation payable for the land acquired by the appellant-University, has been enhanced as under:

1 (i) That the reference court has erred in fixing the market value of the land on the basis of the market value of a small piece of land, as in the instant case 2,361 kanals of land was acquired and the market value of small piece of land could not have been made basis for the purpose of determining the market value of big chunk of a land.
(ii) That the reference court has not taken into consideration that the appellant had provided 120 of kanals to the respondents for construction of their residential houses and each claimant was allotted a plot of 18 marlas of land and one shop site measuring one marla adjacent to the acquired land at the rate of Rs. 9000/- for residential plot and Rs. 5000/- for shop site.

40,000 per kanal for other lands.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.

Before adjudicating the controversy involved in this appeal, this Court deems it proper to observe that the appellant has mainly confined its challenge to the judgment of the learned reference court in respect of enhancement of the market value of culturable land from Rs. 25,000 to 1.5 lacs per kanal.

Even the main thrust of the argument of the learned senior counsel for the appellant was in respect of market value of the culturable land and that the learned reference court did not consider that the land was allotted to the respondents for construction of house and shop, at the rates less than the cost of the acquired land.

7. Brief facts necessary for the disposal of the present appeal are that land measuring 2631 kanals and 14 marlas comprising various survey numbers situated at Village Sira Kotla, Tehsil and District Udhampur was notified for acquisition under section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act (for short the Act) on 04.02.2000 for establishment of Shri Mata Vaishno Devi University and thereafter notification under section 6 of the Act was issued on 07.02.2000.
The acquisition of the land for the purpose of establishment of the University was compulsory in nature.
The Tehsildar, Udhampur was requested to provide average sale rate for the last three years together with the present market rates in the different villages including Sira Kotla.

The Tehsildar, Udhampur conveyed that an average sale rate for village Sira Kotla was Rs. 15,725.20/- per kanal and recommended Rs. 1.00 lac per kanal for culturable land and Rs. 50,000/- per kanal for un-culturable land.
The Tehsildar concerned made the recommendation on the ground that the owners would be rendered homeless and landless due to acquisition.

The Collector visited the spot and found that the village was located on both sides of the Panthal-Domail National Highway Link Road and is three kilometers from Village Bhagata, where Railway Collector had assessed the value of the culturable land and land under houses as Rs. 50,000/- per kanal (aam).
The Collector vide award dated 13.04.2003 fixed the compensation for the acquired land in the following manner:
Culturable
land Rs. 25,000/- per kanal
Banjar Qadeem/Jadeed Rs. 15,000/- per kanal
Gair Mumkin Rs. 10,000/- per kanal 8
. As the acquisition was compulsory in nature, therefore jabrana (solatium) @ 15% of the total value of the land was also awarded.

9. The respondents were not satisfied with the compensation awarded to them by the Collector and as such, they filed an application under Section 18 of the Act for making a reference to the court for determination of the market value of the acquired land.

Accordingly, the matter was referred to the Shri Mata Vaishno Devi University vs Pritam Singh And Others on 7 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57861466/
3 reference court, wherein the appellants filed objections and opposed the reference for enhancement of the compensation.

sentences.text: Respondents, namely, Karan Singh, Krishan Lal and Pritam Singh appeared as witnesses and also examined PWs Jarnail Singh, Sham Lal, Prem Nath and Brijender Singh in support of their claim, whereas the appellant examined Surat Singh, Girdawar.
After examining the evidence, learned reference court enhanced the compensation payable for the acquired land in the manner, as mentioned above.

10. Cross objections have been filed by the respondents, thereby stating that the reference court has erred in granting interest @ 6 per cent per annum for whole of the period, which is against the statute.
It is also stated that the plots were given in undeveloped colonies without civic amenities.

11. The main contention raised by the appellant in the present appeal is that the market value of the land has not been rightly determined by the reference court and without there being any justification, the compensation has been enhanced in an arbitrary manner.
To determine, as to whether the learned reference court has rightly determined the compensation, it is necessary to have a brief resume of the evidence led by the parties.

12. The respondent-claimant, Pritam Singh deposed that the value of the land was not less than Rs.
1,00,000/- per kanal.
The price fixed for their land is very meager and even less than the cost of the land acquired by the Railway Department in Villages Bhagata, Kankunyan, Taleem and Sial.
These villages are adjacent to their village and in fact, the said land was inferior to the land of the Village Sira Kotla.
He also stated that the Jammu- Katra road was close to the acquired land.
During cross-examination, he stated that Katra Town is three kilometers away from the acquired land.
One kanal of land in their village is equal to 13 marlas and the Domel Katra road is about 1  kilometers away and road from Panthal passes through the acquired land.
13. The respondent-claimant, Karan Singh stated that the cost of the acquired land at the time of issuance of notification was more than Rs. 1.00 lac per kanal.
Karnail Singh, Gandharb Singh and one Shanti Devi had sold the land at the rate of Rs. 1.00 lac per kanal.

He has also stated that the Railway Department had paid compensation at the rate of Rs. 50,000/- to Rs. 70,000/- per kanal some 3 to 4 years ago in the villages Bhagata, Kankayan and Taleem, which are adjacent to their village.
During cross- examination, he stated that whole of the land was agricultural land and the road leading to Jammu passes through the middle of the acquired land.
14. The respondent-claimant, KrishanLal stated that the rate of the land was more than Rs. 1.00 lac per kanal.

Karnail Singh, Gandharb and Shanti Devi had sold their land at the above mentioned rate and the Railway Department had paid the compensation at the rate of Rs. 50,000/- per kanal for acquisition of the land in villages Bhagata, Taleem and Kankunyan, which are one kilometer away from the acquired land.
The land acquired by the Railway Department was mostly unculturable and un-irrigated.

During cross-examination, he has stated that 18 marlas of land was given by the Shrine Board for an amount of Rs. 9,000/- for constructing houses and one marla of land for construction of one shop at the rate of Rs. 5,000/-.
Katra is at a distance of 3 kilometers from the acquired land.

It is contended by the appellant that the market value of a small piece of land cannot be considered for the purpose of determining the market value of a large tract of land.

It is mentionable here that this is not an absolute principle of law that for the purpose of determining the market value of a large tract of land, the market value of a small piece of land cannot be taken into consideration.
Rather if comparable instances of sale are not available, then the market value of a small stretch of land can also be taken into consideration for determining the market value of big chunk of land.

22. The Apex Court in "Trishla Jain v. State of Uttaranchal" (2011) 6 SCC 47, has held that the value of small pieces of land can be taken into consideration for determining even the value of the large tract of land but with the condition that while doing so, some deduction is required to be made.

entities.text: Trishla Jain v. State of Uttaranchal" (2011) 6 SCC 47
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Paragraph 39 is relevant, the same is reproduced as under:
"The law with regard to applying the principle of deduction to the determined market value of the acquired land is quite consistent, though, of course, the extent of deduction has varied very widely depending on the facts and circumstances of a given case.
In other words, it is not possible to state precisely the exact deduction which could be made uniformly applicable to all the cases.

Normally the rule stated by this Court consistently, in its different judgments, is that deduction is to be applied on account of carrying out development activities like providing roads or civic amenities such as electricity, water etc. when the land has been acquired for construction of residential, commercial or institutional projects.
It shall also be applied where the sale instances (exemplars) relate to smaller pieces of land and in comparison the acquisition relates to a large tract of land.

In addition thereto, deduction can also be applied on account of wastage of land."
23.

In "Nirmal Singh v. State of Haryana" (2015) 2 SCC 160, it was held by the Honble Supreme Court as under:
"19.

20. The amount of compensation cannot be ascertained with mathematical accuracy.
A comparable instance has to be identified having regard to the proximity from time angle as well as proximity from situation angle.

For determining the market value of the land under acquisition, suitable adjustment has to be made having regard to various positive and negative factors vis--vis the land under acquisition by placing the two in juxtaposition.

they admittedly pertain to small pieces of land.
As per the sale deed executed in favour of respondents witness-Prem Nath, the market value of the land is approximately Rs. 3,333.33/- per marla.
As per the sale deed of the land purchased by Jarnail Singh, the market price of the land comes to Rs. 5000/- per marla.

As per the sale deed of respondents witness, namely, Sham Lal, the cost of land is Rs.
20,000/ per marla.
Thus, as per the sale exemplars placed on record by the respondents-owners, the market value of the land oscillates between Rs. 44,000/ and Rs. 2.60,000/ per kanal (1 kanal =13 marlas).
The difference in the market value of small stretches of land, as noted above, is of such nature that it is very difficult to place reliance upon these sale exemplars.
Some guess is required to be made for estimating the market value of the land.

The Tehsildar, Udhampur had recommended the market value of the culturable land as Rs. 1.00 lac per kanal, but the Collector disagreed with the recommendation that the transaction of small commercial area cannot be the criteria for determining the market value of the large stretch of land and accordingly, determined the market value for the land as mentioned above.

Learned reference court has enhanced the market value of the land on the premise that the Collector though disagreed with the recommendation of the Tehsildar but at the same time, he believed that the respondents would be rendered houseless & landless and under such circumstances, the Collector ought to have fixed the market value of the land @ Rs. 1.00 lac per kanal.

The learned reference court,
after taking into consideration the potential of the development of the land in future,
enhanced the market value of the land.

26. The appellants have placed on record the minutes of the meeting held on 15.12.2023 regarding Kakryal Land Acquisition in respect of proposal for payment of compensation for the acquired land at the rate of Rs. 75,000/- per kanal for culturable and Rs. 40,000 per kanal for other land situated in village Kakryal.

It needs to be noted that the said land was also acquired for the establishment of Shri Mata Vaishno Devi University in the year, 2002 and in that case the Collector had fixed the value of the culturable land as Rs. 25,000/-, for Banjar Qadim/jaded as Rs.
15,000/- and
for Gair Mumkin as Rs. 10,000/-.

In the said case, the reference court enhanced the compensation to Rs. 1,00,000/- per kanal for culturable land, Rs.
50,000/- per kanal for Banjar Jameen/Jadeed land and Rs. 50,000/- per kanal for Gair Mumkin land.

The negotiations ensued between Shri Mata Vaishno Devi University Board and the owners, whereby the efforts were made to settle the compensation payable @ Rs. 75,000/- per kanal for culturable land and Rs. 40,000/-

27. In Trishla Jain's case (supra), the Honble Supreme Court has observed as under:
"45.

This Court, depending on the facts and circumstances of each given case, has taken the view that deduction on account of expenses of development of the sites could vary from 10% to 86.33% depending on the nature of the land, its situation, the purpose and stage of development.

Reference can be made to K.S. Shivadevamma v.
Asstt. Commr. and Land Acquisition Officer [(1996) 2 SCC 62], Ram Piari v. Collector (LA) [(1996) 8 SCC 338] , Chimanlal Hargovind das v. Land Acquisition Officer [(1988) 3 SCC 751] and Hasanali Walimch and v. State of Maharashtra [(1998) 2 SCC 388] ."
28.

sentences.text: No doubt that the land was acquired for the purpose of establishment of university, but it is obvious that the acquired land is to be developed and some expenses would be required to be incurred for developing civic amenities to make it fit for the purpose of the establishment of University.
Therefore, deduction on account of expenses for development of the site is also required to be made from the assessed market value of the land acquired.

The Tehsildar concerned had recommended Rs. 1 lac per kanal for culturable land and as per the sale exemplars market value of the culturable land, oscillates between Rs. 44,000 and Rs. 2,60,000/ per kanal.

Even if, the statements made by the respondents are believed, ignoring the documentary evidence, i.e. the sale exemplars, placed on record by the respondents, the market value of the culturable land was around Rs. 1.00 lac per kanal.
The learned reference court fixed the market value of culturable land @ Rs 1.5 lac per kanal taking into consideration the future potential of development of land.
There appears to be no justification in fixing the market value of the culturable land @ Rs. 1.5 lac per kanal, even if future potential of development is to be taken into consideration.

Be that as it may, by guesstimation, this Court is of the considered view that the market value of the acquired culturable land can be fixed at Rs. 1.00 lac per kanal even after taking into consideration the future prospects of development and by making the deduction at the rate of 15% for development purposes, the respondents are entitled to compensation of Rs. 85,000/- per kanal, as against Rs. 1.50 lac per kanal for culturable land.
As the appellant has not disputed the market value of the banjar qadeem and gair mumkin land determined by the reference court, no interference is warranted.

29. The other contention raised by the appellant is that they had provided 18 marlas and 1 marla of land to the claimants for construction of house and shop, at a cost much less than the cost of the acquired land, is immaterial so far as determining the market value of the land is concerned.
It was the voluntary act of the appellant for the purpose of rehabilitation of the displaced owners and the appellant cannot derive any benefit out of the same.

sentences.text: This Court finds that the learned reference court has not awarded solatium at the rate of 15%, as the acquisition in the present case was compulsory in nature.

In terms of section 23 (2) of the Act,
besides grating the market value of the land in case of compulsory acquisition, an additional sum of Rs. 15% on the market value of the land is also required to be paid.
In case of Ram Mehar's case (supra), it has been held that the additional amount of 15% forms part of the amount of compensation in terms of section 23 of the Act.
31. In view of what has been said and discussed above, the appeal is partly allowed.

The judgment of the reference court is modified, and the appellant is directed to pay the compensation to the respondents for their land acquired, in the following manner:
 Culturable Land Rs. 85,000 per kanal  Banjar Qadim Rs. 50,000/- per kanal
Gair Mumkin RS. 30,000/- per kanal 32.
In addition, the respondents/claimants are held entitled to solatium at the rate of 15% of the market value as determined above.
The interest component awarded by the reference court shall remain the same.
33. Record of the Reference Court be sent back forthwith.
(RAJNESH OSWAL) JUDGE Jammu 07.06.2024

opennyai_summary.arguments:
Aggrieved by the enhancement of the compensation made by the learned reference court, the appellant-Shri Mata Vaishno Devi University has assailed the judgment on the following grounds:
Shri Mata Vaishno Devi University vs Pritam Singh And Others on 7 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57861466/
1 (i) That the reference court has erred in fixing the market value of the land on the basis of the market value of a small piece of land, as in the instant case 2,361 kanals of land was acquired and the market value of small piece of land could not have been made basis for the purpose of determining the market value of big chunk of a land.
(ii) That the reference court has not taken into consideration that the appellant had provided 120 of kanals to the respondents for construction of their residential houses and each claimant was allotted a plot of 18 marlas of land and one shop site measuring one marla adjacent to the acquired land at the rate of Rs. 9000/- for residential plot and Rs. 5000/- for shop site.
that the reference court has not awarded any solatium on the enhanced compensation which the reference court was under obligation to award, as the solatium forms part of the compensation.
11. The main contention raised by the appellant in the present appeal is that the market value of the land has not been rightly determined by the reference court and without there being any justification, the compensation has been enhanced in an arbitrary manner.

(iii) That the land in question falls in Tehsil Katra, whereunder the local revenue system, one kanal comprises of 13 marlas and not 20 marlas, which was the scale applicable in other parts of the erstwhile State of Jammu and Kashmir.
(iv) That the reference court has fixed a higher compensation on the ground that the land acquired by the Railway Authority for construction of a railway station reflected the market value of the acquired land at the time of notification issued under Section 6 of the Land Acquisition Act.
Before adjudicating the controversy involved in this appeal, this Court deems it proper to observe that the appellant has mainly confined its challenge to the judgment of the learned reference court in respect of enhancement of the market value of culturable land from Rs. 25,000 to 1.5 lacs per kanal.
opennyai_summary.facts:
The acquisition of the land for the purpose of establishment of the University was compulsory in nature.
9. The respondents were not satisfied with the compensation awarded to them by the Collector and as such, they filed an application under Section 18 of the Act for making a reference to the court for determination of the market value of the acquired land.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is mentionable here that this is not an absolute principle of law that for the purpose of determining the market value of a large tract of land, the market value of a small piece of land cannot be taken into consideration.
Rather if comparable instances of sale are not available, then the market value of a small stretch of land can also be taken into consideration for determining the market value of big chunk of land.
22. The Apex Court in "Trishla Jain v. State of Uttaranchal" (2011) 6 SCC 47, has held that the value of small pieces of land can be taken into consideration for determining even the value of the large tract of land but with the condition that while doing so, some deduction is required to be made.
For determining the market value of the land under acquisition, suitable adjustment has to be made having regard to various positive and negative factors vis--vis the land under acquisition by placing the two in juxtaposition.

28.
Therefore, deduction on account of expenses for development of the site is also required to be made from the assessed market value of the land acquired.
Even if, the statements made by the respondents are believed, ignoring the documentary evidence, i.e. the sale exemplars, placed on record by the respondents, the market value of the culturable land was around Rs. 1.00 lac per kanal.
The learned reference court fixed the market value of culturable land @ Rs 1.5 lac per kanal taking into consideration the future potential of development of land.
There appears to be no justification in fixing the market value of the culturable land @ Rs. 1.5 lac per kanal, even if future potential of development is to be taken into consideration.
Be that as it may, by guesstimation, this Court is of the considered view that the market value of the acquired culturable land can be fixed at Rs. 1.00 lac per kanal even after taking into consideration the future prospects of development and by making the deduction at the rate of 15% for development purposes, the respondents are entitled to compensation of Rs. 85,000/- per kanal, as against Rs. 1.50 lac per kanal for culturable land.
As the appellant has not disputed the market value of the banjar qadeem and gair mumkin land determined by the reference court, no interference is warranted.
It was the voluntary act of the appellant for the purpose of rehabilitation of the displaced owners and the appellant cannot derive any benefit out of the same.
Shri Mata Vaishno Devi University vs Pritam Singh And Others on 7 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57861466/
9 30.
This Court finds that the learned reference court has not awarded solatium at the rate of 15%, as the acquisition in the present case was compulsory in nature.
In terms of section 23 (2) of the Act,
besides grating the market value of the land in case of compulsory acquisition, an additional sum of Rs. 15% on the market value of the land is also required to be paid.
opennyai_summary.decision:
31. In view of what has been said and discussed above, the appeal is partly allowed.
The judgment of the reference court is modified, and the appellant is directed to pay the compensation to the respondents for their land acquired, in the following manner:
 Culturable Land Rs. 85,000 per kanal  Banjar Qadim Rs. 50,000/- per kanal
Gair Mumkin RS. 30,000/- per kanal 32.
In addition, the respondents/claimants are held entitled to solatium at the rate of 15% of the market value as determined above.
The interest component awarded by the reference court shall remain the same.
33. Record of the Reference Court be sent back forthwith.
